the blends with ethylene elastomers are more stable to the oxidation than neat PA6, but the stability is dependent on elastomer loading and the type of elastomer.

the minor components of polyamide 6 blends are the sources of reactive spots, which are active sites of oxidation and the activation energies calculated for oxidation of PA 6 based blends are the basis for the prediction of long term stability.

the oxidative stability of polyamide 6 is improved by the addition of ethylene elastomers, which are minor components of the blends, and the oxidative stability of the blends is dependent of the loading degree of elastomers and the nature of ethylene elastomer.

the development of polymeric blends for outdoor and radiation applications.
the stability analysis of PA 5/ethylene elastomer blend systems for outdoor and nuclear application.
the development of new polyamide 6 blends with elastomer components for the application of nuclear and outdoor fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the blends with ethylene elastomers, grafted or not, are more sensitive to ageing than neat PA 6.

the blends are more sensitive to oxidation than the neat polyamides, but the elastomer fractions have a stabilizing effect, which is not enough to compensate the negative effect of elastomer radicals.
PA 6 is a most stable polymer in the blends with elastomers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the blends are stable enough for outdoor and nuclear fields of application.
the oxidative stability of the PA 6 based blend is improved by the addition of elastomer components and that the elastomer fraction is the key parameter for the promotion of oxidation.
the oxidative degradation is promoted by the presence of elastomers, which act as radical sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the blends with ethylene elastomers are more stable than the neat PA 6 and the blends with ethylenic elastomers grafted with male anhydride are less sensitive to oxidation than the pristine elastomers.
the oxidative stability of the polyamide 6 is significantly affected by the presence of elastomers, and that the stability can be improved by a proper choice of the elastomer and its loading.
the oxidative stability of polyamide 6 can be improved by the use of elastomeric components, which are minor components of the blends.
